title: Data policies (DLP) for Copilot Studio agents
summary: The page is held because its policy-management automation entry is a labelled list of cmdlets rather than a runnable PowerShell call: creation and updates omit required parameters. The connector mappings, enforcement behaviour and endpoint-filtering command are documented; some supporting guidance needs qualifications or citations.

claims.where: What it is; summary
claims.claim: Data policies govern which connectors apps, flows and agents can use together.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways to help reduce risk in your organization.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Microsoft also calls these data loss prevention (DLP) policies.
claims.quote: based on the allow and deny patterns configured in the data loss prevention (DLP) policy.

claims.where: What it is; controls[0]
claims.claim: The policy data groups are Business, Non-Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: The three data groups are the Business data group, the Non-Business data group, and the Blocked data group.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Connectors in different groups cannot share data.
claims.quote: The key point is that connectors in the same group can share data in Microsoft Power Platform, whereas connectors in different groups can't share data.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: An app or flow cannot combine SharePoint in Business with Gmail in Non-Business.
claims.quote: if you place SharePoint and Salesforce connectors in the Business group and you place Gmail in the Non-Business group, makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: A Blocked connector cannot be used where the policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Data policy enforcement has been in effect for all tenants since early 2025.
claims.quote: Since early 2025, data policy enforcement is in effect for all tenants

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Agents cannot be exempted from data policy enforcement since March 2025.
claims.quote: Since March 2025, agents can't be exempted from data policy enforcement. It's no longer possible to exempt agents with a PowerShell command.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Virtual connectors are not based on a REST API.
claims.quote: Virtual connectors are connectors that appear in data policies for administrators to control, but they're not based on a RESTful API.

claims.where: What it is; summary
claims.claim: Copilot Studio capabilities, including tools, channels and triggers, are governed through these policies.
claims.quote:
Require user authentication
- Block using Power Platform connectors as tools
- Block HTTP requests
- Block Azure Bot Service skills
- Block publishing to specific channels
- Block event triggers

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments covered by their scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Add all environments gives tenant-wide coverage.
claims.quote: Add all environments: Adds all the environments in your entire tenant. This policy automatically applies to any new environment created in the tenant.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check: compare scopes
claims.claim: Tenant-level policies can include or exclude selected environments.
claims.quote: Tenant-level policies can be defined to include or exclude specific environments.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Learn says connectors introduced after 2019, such as unauthenticated chat and Direct Line, are likely to be in default Non-business.
claims.quote: Connectors introduced after 2019, such as Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio or Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio, are likely to be part of the default "Non-business" group.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Learn says many organisations automatically block connectors in Non-business.
claims.quote: In many organizations, connectors in the "Non-business" group are automatically blocked.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that blocking new connectors by default can cause production outages affecting Direct Line or unauthenticated website agents.
claims.quote: Misaligned configurations, such as data policies blocking new connectors by default, could result in production outages. For example, essential features like Direct Line or unauthenticated agent deployments on websites might be unexpectedly blocked.

Follow the sequence shown in your admin centre.' Both cited guides were read and give different sequences.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy (create); Get-DlpPolicy (list); Set-DlpPolicy (update policy details such as the display name) is the supplied policy-management automation call.
claims.quote:
Set-DlpPolicy
    -PolicyName <String>
    -UpdatedPolicy <Object>
    [-ApiVersion <String>]
    [<CommonParameters>]
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api.call with 'Get-DlpPolicy', retaining its existing docs URL, and append to the row note 'Automation shown lists policies only.' The listed cmdlets and descriptions exist, but parenthetical descriptions are not executable arguments. Set-DlpPolicy requires -PolicyName and -UpdatedPolicy; New-DlpPolicy requires -NewPolicy or -DisplayName and -EnvironmentType, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powerapps.administration.powershell/new-dlppolicy. Do not print the current labelled list as a runnable call.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table

claims.quote:
Select the three dots (⋮) next to the connector, and then:

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Maker guidance is reached through Copilot > Settings > Copilot Studio > Maker guidance > environment or environment group > Edit setting.
claims.quote: In the panel, select the environments or environment groups you want to configure a custom guidance message for. Select Edit setting at the bottom of the panel to confirm your choice.
claims.fix: Keep the path supported by the cited Agent status page, but append: 'The separate admin guide calls the Review-pane control Maker guidelines, restricts it to Managed Environments and uses Edit rule for environment groups; see https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/maker-guidelines.' This reports the differing documentation rather than silently choosing one. The pre-check's missing phrase is not a path error: selecting environments or environment groups is explicitly documented.

claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing limits control how makers share agents.

That page states 'Sharing limits only apply to agents that require authentication.' This is the supporting Microsoft page missing from the concept's source list.
